clues.grass: Older fishers say the bay stayed calm while the meadow lived.
clues.dune: Where the dunes had worn away, the sea walked straight in.
clues.sort: Crews pulled bags of rubbish from the street drains for days.
clues.light: With no power for a week, another family left.
clues.meet: One street's planting stopped at the fence, and the sea found the rest.

papers.headline: The waves are coming closer
papers.story: The storm passed and the water never reached the door. Older fishers remember when the bay stayed calm, before the meadow thinned.

papers.headline: Water at the doorstep
papers.story: The water came over the doorstep and stood for two days. Fishers say the waves have grown as the meadow thinned.

papers.headline: No calm left in the bay
papers.story: Deep water filled the front rooms and stayed. The waves now roll over the bare sand where the meadow once lay.

papers.headline: The sea keeps its distance
papers.story: The water stayed off the shore road. The meadow is thinner than the fishers remember, and it still holds the waves back.

papers.headline: The waves come further in
papers.story: The water crossed the doorstep and stayed inside. The meadow is thin now, and the fishers miss the calm bay.

papers.headline: The meadow is gone
papers.story: Deep water kept the street for a week, and the last homes emptied. The bay lies bare, and the waves come all the way in.

papers.headline: The dunes are wearing thin
papers.story: The storm stayed out at sea this time. Last winter it came through the gap where the dunes had worn away.

papers.headline: Sea walks through the gap
papers.story: The storm came through where the dunes had worn away. The water came up into the front rooms and stood for two days.

papers.headline: The sea takes the low road
papers.story: Deep water ran through the gap and homes went under. The dunes had worn to almost nothing.

papers.headline: A calm sea, a wider gap
papers.story: The storm blew itself out at sea. The gap in the dunes is wide enough to walk through now.

papers.headline: The gap lets the sea in
papers.story: The sea came through the gap, and the front rooms stayed wet for two days. Neighbours stacked sandbags on the bare shore.

papers.headline: Where the dunes used to be
papers.story: Deep water came through the bare gap, and the street emptied. The sand that once held the sea is gone.

papers.headline: The drains run slow
papers.story: The street stayed dry through the storm. The drains ran slow all the same, half full of rubbish.

papers.headline: Street drains choke again
papers.story: Crews pulled bags of rubbish from the drains. The water lay inside the homes for two days.

papers.headline: The drains gave up
papers.story: Deep water sat in the street all week, and families moved away one by one. The drains were packed solid.

papers.headline: Dry street, full grates
papers.story: The rain fell and the road stayed clear. The corner grates sit full of rubbish, waiting for a heavier storm.

papers.headline: The water has nowhere to go
papers.story: The storm water stood in the front rooms for two days. The drains were choked with rubbish before it even began.

papers.headline: A street under standing water
papers.story: Deep water covered the road for a week, and the homes stood empty. The drains have been choked for years.

papers.headline: The lights come and go
papers.story: The storm went by and the street kept dry. The power went out for a night, and the street lamps with it.

papers.headline: Dark street, empty street
papers.story: With no power for a week, another family left. The water came into the front rooms, and the lamps stayed off.

papers.headline: The last lights go out
papers.story: Deep water took the homes on the low road. The power poles went down with them, and nobody came to mend the wires.

papers.headline: The lights held, mostly
papers.story: The storm passed with the street still dry, and the lights held. The power still dips most evenings.

papers.headline: A week of dark evenings
papers.story: The power has been off for a week, and more families have gone. The water lay in the front rooms the whole time.

papers.headline: The street went dark for good
papers.story: The last families left the dark houses to the water. Nobody has mended the power line since the storm took it.

papers.headline: A patchwork shore
papers.story: The storm never came ashore. Some houses planted their strip of shore, and the rest left theirs bare.

papers.headline: One street can't hold a bay
papers.story: Next door's planting stopped at the fence, and the sea found the rest. The water lay indoors for two days.

papers.headline: The fence was not enough
papers.story: The sea came over every patch that stood alone, homes and all. The street went quiet, and the fences mark nothing now.

papers.headline: The shore, house by house
papers.story: The bay lay quiet all summer. Each house still minds its own patch, and the gaps between them show.

papers.headline: Help that stops at the fence
papers.story: The sea came through where the planting ended. The water sat in the houses for two days, and next door stayed dry.

papers.headline: Alone, the street went under
papers.story: The sea took the homes one fence at a time, until none were left. The street might have held together.

papers.headline: The wall holds
papers.story: The storm pushed all night and the wall did not move. The sea stayed on its side of the stone.

papers.headline: The wall held, the rain came in
papers.story: The wall held the sea back all night. The rain found the low front rooms and stayed for two days.

papers.headline: High water behind the wall
papers.story: The sea never got past the wall. The rain filled the low street for days, and families moved to higher ground.

papers.headline: The sea has been kind
papers.story: The wall fell years ago, and nobody ever repaired it. The water kept off the street all the same.

papers.headline: The wall nobody mended
papers.story: Years went by without a single repair, and the wall gave way in the night. The street lay under the sea for two days.

papers.headline: The wall that everyone forgot
papers.story: Nobody had paid to repair it in years. It went in one night, and the deep water emptied the street by morning.

papers.headline: A quiet year on the shore
papers.story: The storm came and went. The street slept dry.

papers.headline: The water came and went
papers.story: The water reached the front rooms, and it stayed for two days. Neighbours helped each other carry the furniture up the stairs.

papers.headline: Still here
papers.story: The deep water left the street to the gulls. The neighbours who stayed share supper on the high road.

papers.headline: A good year by the water
papers.story: The boats came home full, and the sea kept to itself. Neighbours repainted their shutters in the good weather.

papers.headline: The water rises, so do we
papers.story: The water came up over the doorstep and took two days to leave. Neighbours gave each other dry rooms until it drained away.

papers.headline: The high road holds
papers.story: The deep water claimed the homes on the shore road. The families who stayed gather on the high road on clear evenings.
